title: Blameless postmortems, action items, and what makes them actually get done

videos.script: Two days after the double charge, the Billing team sits down to write about it. {{sit}} The obvious question is who. Who wrote the retry. Who approved it. Who released it on the busiest afternoon of the month. {{who}} Answer that, and the meeting is over in five minutes, and nothing changes. {{over}} The better question is how. How did it make sense, at the time, to do each of those things? And what would have caught it? {{how}} Ask it that way, and you find six threads, not one. And you find that three of the fixes were agreed months ago, and never done. {{threads}} This lesson is about the blameless postmortem. The document, the meeting, and the action items that decide whether any of it was worth the time. {{lesson}}
